observations: Photos show a single used automatic transmission/gearbox unit, heavily soiled with grime and old grease.
No manufacturer plate, part number, or barcode sticker is legible in any photo.
A wiring harness connector is seen hanging loose/cut in photo 1 with exposed colored wires.
Blue paint marker dab visible on casing in photo 0 and photo 2, possibly a yard/stock mark, not informative.
Unit sits directly on a dirty workshop floor; no test bench, stand, or rig is shown.
No vehicle, engine bay, or donor car is shown to confirm make, model, or application.
A watermark 'GOD OF ABRAHAM INVESTMENT' overlays all three photos; this is a seller/reseller stamp, not proof of anything.
Seller's new message is text only, repeating prior claims with no new photo or video evidence.

claims.claim: Dealer in all kinds of Japanese parts and gearbox
claims.evidence: General business claim in text; no shop signage or inventory shown in photos.
No shipping label, container photo, or import document shown.

claims.claim: Tested and working (reaffirmed: 'I tested it myself yesterday')
claims.evidence: Still no test bench photo, gauge reading, or video clip of the gearbox shifting/engaging; a verbal reassurance is not visual proof.
This is an audio/operational claim; no video or sound clip provided.
No odometer, donor vehicle, or service sticker is visible; mileage cannot be read off a standalone gearbox.
Casing bolts and seams are caked in grime in all 3 photos, obscuring whether seals or bolt heads show tamper marks.

claims.claim: 'Please check again' / 'everything I said is true'
claims.evidence: A plain assertion with no accompanying new photo, video, or document; treated as seller's word only.

risks.risk: Make/model/engine application of the gearbox is unknown, which drives price far more than condition.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the ID/VIN-type tag or stamped part number plate usually riveted or stamped on the case, or the donor vehicle it was pulled from.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced as a specific fitment; would need to be priced as an unidentified generic used gearbox, which is effectively not price-able without this data

risks.risk: Internal wear (clutch packs, solenoids, torque converter) cannot be assessed from exterior photos.
risks.proof: A video clip of the unit running on a test bench with clear shifting between gears, or a stall-test clip.

risks.risk: Loose/cut wiring harness connector seen in photo 1 may indicate prior damage or incomplete harness.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the connector showing it is intact and properly terminated, plus confirmation all sensor pigtails are present.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having a damaged/incomplete wiring harness, lowering value

risks.risk: Seal and gasket condition (oil leaks) is hidden under heavy grime.
risks.proof: Photo of cleaned mating surfaces and pan gasket area, or video showing no fluid seepage after a bench test.

risks.risk: 'Tokunbo/Belgium' origin claim cannot be checked, which matters for buyer trust on condition grading.
risks.proof: Photo of shipping manifest, container tag, or original import paperwork.
risks.if_unproven: treated as an unverifiable origin claim, no premium applied for 'direct import' grading

proof_requests: Clear close-up of any stamped part number / ID plate on the gearbox case.
Statement or photo of the exact donor vehicle (make, model, year, engine code) this gearbox was removed from.
Video clip of the gearbox on a test bench or test stand showing it turning/shifting without noise, dated or timestamped.
Close-up of the wiring harness connector seen hanging in photo 1.
Photo of the case after wiping down the main seams/bolts to check for prior opening or leaks.
response.reason: The seller's reply is a verbal reassurance with no new photo or video, so the fitment-critical identity and the 'tested/working' claim remain unverified; a worst-case price still cannot be set without a readable part number or test footage.
